purpose.summary: Retain bounded fixed-size records for confirmed transactions in the volatile Chronik observer without assigning validation or consensus authority.
scope: Retain transaction ID, block position, serialized size, a non-cryptographic payload fingerprint, observed-family flags, diagnostic counts, and CashTokens-prefix output count for each confirmed transaction in the active suffix.

Compute each debug-only block fingerprint once and compose projection fingerprints from at most 288 cached block values so public tests can compare connect, disconnect, restart, reindex, pruning, and bounded-eviction state.
Keep records volatile, reversible, and bounded by the existing 288-block suffix.
Preserve compile-time default OFF, runtime default OFF, explicit local-regtest-only opt-in, and observe/index-only operation.
exclusions: No consensus, validation, mempool, chain-selection, activation, chain-parameter, testnet, mainnet, P2P, RPC, wallet, or user-interface rule changes.
No transaction bodies, inputs, outputs, prevouts, token identifiers, balances, UTXO relationships, persistence, database, file format, API, socket, service, or thread.
No token-validity, cryptographic-commitment, stable-API, or security claim for the retained diagnostics or FNV fingerprints.
No local binary, build cache, raw process output, absolute host path, parent environment, operator material, private history, or unrelated product material enters this change.

files.test_reachability: Defines the exact retained fields, bounded lifetime, fingerprint purpose, and excluded authority.

files.production_reachability: Compiled only in the optional local-regtest observer; stores fixed records after node validation and returns no validation decision.
files.test_reachability: Adds fixed-record retention, cached block commitments, consistency checks, and exact per-position non-zero asset-field units.

files.production_reachability: Extends the private optional-observer ABI and debug logs only; callbacks remain post-validation and void.
files.test_reachability: Publishes block and projection record fingerprints to the public functional oracle.
Independently recomputes ordered record commitments across connect, every deep post-eviction disconnect, restart, full reindex, chainstate reindex, and recovery.
Independently recomputes the exact pruned bootstrap commitment and the bounded projection after the next connected block.

commands: Build with both Chronik options OFF and run inherited legacy mining.
expected_results: No Chronik link edge enters bitcoind and legacy behavior remains unchanged.

commands: Build with BUILD_CHRONIK_OBSERVER=ON, omit -chronikobserver, and run mining_basic.py.
expected_results: The optional library is linked but no observer starts and inherited mining passes.

commands: Run check-chronik-observer and feature_chronik_block_observer.py with --hermetic-child-env on a fresh datadir.
expected_results: Focused units and all bounded record-reconstruction scenarios pass.

scenarios.command: Start the compiled-in observer only on isolated regtest and connect, disconnect, and reconsider confirmed blocks.
expected_results: Debug commitments match independent reconstruction while the node tip remains authoritative.
failure_conditions: Any non-regtest activation, commitment mismatch, state mutation on rejection, or validation influence fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Restart the observer after building a retained active-chain suffix.
expected_results: Startup atomically adopts the exact ordered retained-record commitment without minting live events.
failure_conditions: Partial adoption, stale records, wrong order, wrong commitment, or growth beyond 288 blocks fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run a fresh full reindex process at height 288.
expected_results: Ordered block-file callbacks rebuild the exact last-288-block record projection and its independent commitment.
failure_conditions: Missing, duplicated, reordered, rejected, or mismatched records fail the scenario.

scenarios.command: Run a fresh chainstate reindex process at height 288.
expected_results: Ordered chainstate callbacks rebuild the exact last-288-block record projection without changing the active tip or UTXO-set hash.
failure_conditions: Bootstrap masking, block-file reindex, changed chain state, callback divergence, or mismatched records fail the scenario.

scenarios.command: Restart explicit observer opt-in on the inherited physically pruned height-1001 datadir.
expected_results: The exact still-readable 288-block suffix reconstructs with its independently checked record commitment, and the next connection preserves the bound.
failure_conditions: Unreadable retained bodies, wrong suffix, event minting, record mismatch, or bound growth fails the scenario.

scenarios.command: Disconnect through the retained anchor, reject continuation, and restart for reconstruction.
expected_results: Records roll back LIFO, the observer fails closed beyond its anchor, and restart reconstructs the active suffix.
failure_conditions: Non-LIFO acceptance, mutation after rebuild-required, unbounded retention, or node consensus influence fails the scenario.

platforms: Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 public verification after technical acceptance

limitations: Projection fingerprints are non-cryptographic debug commitments composed from at most 288 cached per-block fingerprints on each event.
Memory is bounded by 288 consensus-bounded blocks but grows with the confirmed transaction count inside that suffix.
The functional commitment oracle uses ordinary zero-asset coinbase transactions; focused units independently assert each non-zero observed-family record field, txid, and block position.
No transaction body, prevout, durable state, historical full-chain index, mempool view, or query interface is retained.
Local tests are contradiction checks only; no result is public reproduction evidence at record-review time.
counterevidence: No public build or functional execution of the exact candidate exists at record-review time.
A matching FNV commitment does not establish cryptographic integrity, transaction validity, token validity, or consensus correctness.
Restart and reindex reconstruction do not demonstrate persistence, crash recovery, historical queries, or production API compatibility.
The unchanged default path remains authoritative: Chronik is compiled out or runtime disabled unless explicitly enabled on local regtest.
